difficulty.official: No formal official difficulty grade found in STF/Naturkartan API fields for this section.
difficulty.summary: STF treats this as a 14 km, 4-5 hour mountain stage. Naturkartan/Länsstyrelsen gives 14.0 km and 4-6 hours. Field reports describe a moderate rolling mountain day that becomes harder in wet, foggy or shoulder-season conditions because of open mountain, boggy ground, repeated ascent/descent and seasonal insects.

Field reports mention occupied lakeside spots and a 2024 camp by a bridge/brook north of Servvejávrri. Treat these as route-context clues, not importable campsite POIs.
Higher camps may reduce mosquito pressure compared with low, wet, lakeside/birch areas.

closureDecision.summary: No official Länsstyrelsen notice was found that closes or reroutes the Serve-Tärnasjö summer hiking section. Do not import as closed.

protectedArea.name: Vindelfjällen nature reserve / Natura 2000 context
protectedArea.summary: The section lies inside Vindelfjällen. Public rules prohibit damaging natural features, disturbing wildlife, disturbing reindeer husbandry and off-route motorized travel. Natura 2000 permission rules concern activities or works that may significantly affect the area, not ordinary low-impact hiking.

currentNotices.summary: Länsstyrelsen began removing winter route poles early due snow/thaw: much bare ground, thawing streams, but still snow in higher terrain. This affects winter navigation and shoulder-season travel, not a summer hiking closure.
New bridge over Juktån at Rasteselet; relevant as a Vindelfjällen bridge notice but off this exact section.
currentNotices.importImplication: do not attach as section-24 closure

currentNotices.summary: Snowmobile routes near Umasjö/Jirestugan and Norra Fjällnäs/Syterstugan closed effective 2026-04-28. Winter/snowmobile route notice only.
currentNotices.importImplication: do not import as summer hiking closure

weatherAndFire.smhiSnapshot: On 2026-04-30, SMHI point warnings for Serve and Tärnasjö showed no inner point warning, but broader/outer grass-fire message was present. Forecast snapshot included fog/poor visibility and possible snow showers by 2026-05-02.
weatherAndFire.fire: Check live fire-ban status before any fire. No static section-specific ban should be imported from the 2026-04-30 snapshot.

dogsReindeerHuntingFishing: National dog-control period 1 March-20 August was active on 2026-04-30. In Vindelfjällen, dogs should be leashed/closely controlled to avoid disturbing reindeer and wildlife.
Reindeer calving and sensitivity are especially important in April-June; no hiking closure for this section was found.

Small-game hunting on state mountain land starts 25 August; 25 August-15 September is Sweden-resident only, then 16 September-15 March for all with permit. Treat as seasonal user-conflict/safety note, not closure.

Tärnasjön has a specific fishing restriction from Lenasuolo to Rasjekukkes inflow: fishing only 1 July-31 August, quota 100 fishing-days/year, permit via Naturum Vindelfjällen Hemavan. Add only if water/fishing metadata is in scope.
hutSeasons: STF Serve 2026 opening periods: 27 February-3 May and 18 June-20 September.
STF Tärnasjö 2026 opening periods: 27 February-3 May and 18 June-20 September.
On 2026-04-30 both huts were in late winter opening period; summer service starts 2026-06-18.
safetyNotes: Open mountain over Servvetjåhkka can be foggy/windy despite no technical scrambling.
Wetlands and boggy ground are a durable route theme; boardwalk conditions should be rechecked but no current closure was found.
Mobile coverage is poor at Tärnasjö hut, but sources note better chances on the point, on the trail above Stáinnavarrie or up toward Serve.

conditionReports.summary: Calls the stage moderate and deceptively long: rolling rather than steep, with trail often staying on hillsides to avoid boggy lower ground. Notes Norra Storfjället views and Tärnasjö hut in blueberry/birch forest.

Up/down but not steep; forest, treeline, tall grass/rocks, lakes, reindeer and 15-20 people. Planned lake camp was occupied, so camped higher. Important service caveat: Serve shop was unexpectedly closed.
Strong July mosquito/horsefly note at Serve. Climb over Servvetjåhkka rewarded by views, followed by wetter terrain and bog/boardwalk balancing. Walking time around 3 h 14 min.
GPS measured 14.2 km. Initial climb about 200 m, then gradual descent. Trail very well marked with cairns/orange marks. Boardwalks over wettest areas but otherwise bog-wet in places.

16 km including approach/variant, 09:00-14:45. Humid low-cloud morning; many streams available for drinking; late-season warning about darker/colder days and hut closures. Mosquito index zero in September.

Reverse direction. After Tärnasjö, continued toward Serve and camped by a bridge/brook north of Servvejávrri before the last up/down toward Serve; bathing possible. Next day: phone reception on high point before Serve.
Lists 13.8 km, 384 m gain, 4-4.5 h, hard, 4.4 rating. 2025 reviews mention good views/conditions and not crowded. Caveat: incorrectly associates Tärnasjö archipelago bridges with this section.

Community notes praise Tärnasjö common area/kitchens and lakeside sauna; Serve noted as having a common area. Treat generic small-shop language cautiously because current STF does not list Serve shop.

Useful durable caveat: low-lying lakes/wetlands can mean heavy summer mosquitoes, and higher camping may reduce bugs. Notes no sauna at Serve and that Tärnasjö boat service for the next section has been discontinued since 2017.
